what: Host-side timing of eldpc on a Sapphire Rapids-W workstation CPU with an NVIDIA L40S: host ISA A/B (AVX-512 against AVX2), core variant A/B (ELDPC_DEVICE_CLASS default against ada64), bb288 z at the default 1 ms cadence gap, and 10 ms cadence runs. Every number is read from bench/bench.py results.json files (one directory per run, run ids below).

machine.note: the GPU power limit and clocks are in machine_state_before_after_each_job (nvidia-smi before and after every job); no other GPU process was seen in any of them

recipe.description: [[288,12,18]] bivariate bicycle code, 18 rounds, Z basis

method.ab_design: two sides set by an environment variable, so each run is its own bench.py process (ELDPC_ISA is read when the library loads; bench.py creates both handles of a pair in one process under one ELDPC_DEVICE_CLASS value). Blocks in ABBA order (block 1 and 4 one side, 2 and 3 the other); each run is a full-length single-config bench.py measurement with its own A/A control (6 sessions x 1500 calls per handle).
method.block_value: the pooled statistic of handle A of the run (9000 timed calls)
method.difference: mean of the block values of each side, second side minus first; ratios = the two means divided either way (computed)
method.spreads: max_block_spread_within_side_us = largest (max - min) of one side's block values; max_abs_in_run_aa_band_us = largest |end| of any run's A/A band (range of the per-session A/A differences) over the runs of both sides; closest_blocks_gap_us = the nearest pair of blocks of the two sides (positive/negative in the direction of the difference when every block of one side lies beyond every block of the other)
method.per_session: runs.json holds every run's pooled statistics, A/A band and per-session A/A differences; this file keeps the bands
